sounds.name: Whoosh, fast and medium
sounds.description: A quick, clean swish of air with a defined middle.

sync.how: Ease-in-out: put the sync point at the middle of the move. Ease-out (fast start, slowing to a stop): about a quarter of the way in. Ease-in (slow start, fast exit): about three quarters of the way in.

adapt.notes: To fit a move up to about 15% shorter or 20% longer, play it faster or slower (its pitch moves with it); beyond that, use the next speed. Adjust level with gain, but for a clearly softer or harder sound use the other intensity rather than a big gain change.

pairs_with.how: Something landing: the whoosh on the move (its sync point at the move's fastest point) and the impact on the frame it lands. A whoosh that suits the move's length dies away just before the landing; use one a step softer than the impact.
Something arriving and appearing: the whoosh during the move, the pop as it lands, at a lower gain than the whoosh.
A reveal: the whoosh into the reveal, the shimmer starting at the whoosh's sync point.

sounds.name: Letter key, firm
use_for: Building your own typing to match on-screen text
avoid_for: Long runs of typing (use a typing run)

sync.how: Put the sync point on the frame the character appears.

adapt.notes: For your own typing, place single keys per character with uneven gaps (±30%) and a little gain variation (±1.5 dB).

pairs_with.how: Pressing Enter to send or submit: the Return key, then a button click 80–150 ms later.
A message being typed and sent: the typing run, then a message-out sound.

sounds.name: Return key, firm
sounds.description: A firm, decisive Return: send, submit, done.
use_for: Pressing Enter to send, submit or search
The end of a typed line
avoid_for: Long runs of typing (use a typing run)

sync.how: Put the sync point on the frame the character appears.

adapt.notes: For your own typing, place single keys per character with uneven gaps (±30%) and a little gain variation (±1.5 dB).

pairs_with.how: Pressing Enter to send or submit: the Return key, then a button click 80–150 ms later.
A message being typed and sent: the typing run, then a message-out sound.

sounds.name: Chalk drawing
sounds.description: Chalk on a blackboard, drawing a few long strokes.
use_for: Lines, arrows, shapes and diagrams being drawn
avoid_for: Loud moments: it's a quiet, close sound

sync.how: Start it as the line starts to draw; trim or fade to the length of the stroke.

adapt.notes: For longer writing, chain two runs with a short gap; for shorter, fade the end at a gap between strokes.

pairs_with.how: Items written in turn: each word or line with its step tone at −6 dB.

sounds.name: Coin drop
sounds.description: A coin dropped on a table: it rings, bounces and rattles flat.
use_for: A saving or a small payment
Tips, change, a coin of the realm
One coin landing on a graph or pile
avoid_for: Abstract money moments that are better as a chart or a number (use data sounds)

sync.how: Sync point on the frame the coin lands.

adapt.notes: Small rate changes only: the coins' pitch moves with the rate.

pairs_with.how: A total counting up: the count-up, then the register or a coin drop as it lands.
